correctness.rationale: The exact uniform-attachment update changes the degree-profile polynomial by 1+(z−1)z^r. Conditional covariance with the root attachment indicator gives recurrence (1), which is independently checked against exhaustive parent arrays through size 9. The finite unary identity follows by exact coefficient extraction and summation; strict signs at sizes 21 and 22 plus the positive difference for n≥7 prove the complete threshold. For fixed k, geometric profile means and vanishing root degree-k probabilities make the covariances a Cesàro recurrence with limit 2^{−k−1}. All critical hypotheses and endpoint n=2 were checked; 637 exact assertions pass, but tests are only finite corroboration.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the finite sign reversal at 22 vertices and the unscaled mixed covariance between the distinguished root degree and every fixed global outdegree count. The closest complete source, Janson (2005), establishes the limiting degree frequencies and covariances between global count variables, not a distinguished-root cross moment; no implication to the stated sign threshold is available from those results. Full arXiv text of Backhausz–Móri and Acan–Hitczenko was inspected and treats, respectively, fixed tree levels and a different plane-oriented model. The prior exact root-degree/leaf covariance covers only degree zero; that special case is expressly not novel. Search failures do not certify historical uniqueness, particularly given the inaccessible 1992 Mahmoud–Smythe full text.
residual_risks: The 1992 Mahmoud–Smythe paper could not be examined in full; an implicit root-degree mixed moment might occur in its appendices or formulas.

value.rationale: The number of unary vertices is a canonical part of the degree profile of a growing rooted tree, and its correlation with founder branching reverses sharply at exactly 22 vertices. The geometric cross-covariance profile for every fixed degree uncovers a structured founder effect not described by bulk profile CLTs, and the finite conservation identity sum_k Cov(D,N_k)=0 shows why high-degree contributions must offset these positive limits. This is a motivated joint-statistic classification with a nontrivial finite boundary and limit, not a numerical table or a routine restatement of degree frequencies.
